record.paper_title: Recent Results and Open Problems in Evolutionary Multiobjective Optimization
record.original_question: What stopping criteria can reliably decide when a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm should terminate, so that parameterless MOEAs can stop based on convergence or lack of improvement rather than an externally fixed iteration budget?

evidence.quote: Another missing mechanism to get to a parameterless MOEA is a well-established stopping criterion.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA) that maintains, at each generation $t \in \mathbb{N}$, a finite population $P_t \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and evaluates each individual under a vector objective $F : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^m$ ($m \ge 2$), producing a non-dominated front $\mathcal{F}_t \subset \mathbb{R}^m$ (with respect to Pareto dominance). Assume the goal of the algorithm is to approximate the true Pareto front $\mathcal{P}^* \subset \mathbb{R}^m$ of $F$ in both convergence and diversity.

A stopping criterion is a measurable function
$$ S : \big(\mathcal{F}_1, \mathcal{F}_2, \dots, \mathcal{F}_t\big) \mapsto \{0,1\} \quad (t = 1, 2, \dots), $$
where output $1$ signals termination at generation $t$. A stopping criterion is called parameterless if its definition involves no user-supplied tolerances, window sizes, confidence levels, or maximum-generation budgets that depend on the unknown problem instance.

Design and justify a parameterless stopping criterion $S$ with the following properties, or prove that no such criterion exists in this generality:

(1) Soundness: there exist problem-independent constants such that, whenever $S$ outputs $1$ at generation $t$, the produced approximation $\mathcal{F}_t$ has, with high probability, achieved either (a) provable convergence to $\mathcal{P}^*$ in a chosen quality indicator (e.g.\ hypervolume, inverted generational distance, or $\epsilon$-indicator), or (b) certified lack of further improvement, in the sense that $\sup_{s \ge t} I(\mathcal{F}_s) - I(\mathcal{F}_t)$ is below a tolerance derived intrinsically from observed history.

(2) Completeness: on every problem instance for which the underlying MOEA is convergent in distribution to $\mathcal{P}^*$, $S$ terminates in finite expected time.

(3) Universality: the criterion uses only the sequence $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t\ge 1}$ (and possibly population data) and does not require an externally fixed iteration budget or instance-specific tuning.

Determine whether such a criterion is achievable, and if so, exhibit one and analyze its statistical guarantees on the front-to-front improvement process.
artifact.status_search_result: Several stopping criteria for MOEAs have been proposed (e.g., the MGBM criterion combining the mutual domination rate with a Kalman-filter-based evidence-gathering process, statistical-testing-based convergence criteria, and taxonomies of online stopping rules), and recent benchmarking efforts continue to evaluate them. However, no proposal is universally accepted as a reliable, fully parameterless stopping criterion that works across arbitrary instances, and the question of establishing such a well-grounded criterion is still regarded as an open challenge in the EMO community.

status_evidence.title: Benchmarking Stopping Criteria for Evolutionary Multi-objective Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Stopping criteria... have attracted little attention in the EMO community; benchmarking different proposals is still needed.
status_evidence.claim: Stopping criteria for MOEAs remain an active research topic without a universally accepted solution.

status_evidence.title: An Approach to Stopping Criteria for MOEAs: The MGBM Criterion
status_evidence.snippet: MGBM combines the mutual domination rate with a simplified Kalman filter for evidence gathering.
status_evidence.claim: Specific criteria like MGBM exist but rely on parameters and are not universally established.

status_evidence.title: A Taxonomy of Online Stopping Criteria for Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: Survey/taxonomy of online stopping criteria for MOEAs.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple competing proposals indicate the problem of a reliable parameterless criterion is unresolved.
